transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. Um, I hope I can give you the right information today. 

I guess I'm mostly here because... well, my wife and my director at work sort of asked me to come. I've just been really, really driven lately. I mean, it's a good thing to be motivated, right? But I guess I've been launching a ton of new projects all at once. Like, drafting these massive new work plans, scheduling myself for a bunch of new IT certifications, completely upgrading our home network, messaging a lot of old contacts... just trying to get ahead and be productive, you know? 

But I guess it gets a little intense for the people around me. I sort of just keep going and blow past normal limits until my wife or my boss has to actually step in and tell me to stop. I really don't mean to cause any trouble or worry anyone, I just get really focused on getting things done. Does that make sense?
Have you ever had periods in the past where your mood was very low or depressed, or times when you felt hopeless or lost interest in things you normally enjoy?

Well, um... I guess everyone gets a little down sometimes, right? It's probably just normal stress from trying to do so much. But, yeah, I suppose there are stretches where... where I just wake up feeling kind of like a failed version of myself. 

It's not that bad, really, just this heavy, flat feeling. Like, even answering my wife's normal questions about the day just feels like it's asking too much of me. I try not to let it show because I don't want to be a burden, and I know I should be grateful for everything I have. I hope that's the kind of thing you were asking about? I don't want to make it sound worse than it is, I just... I do get into these slumps sometimes. Is that pretty common for someone in my line of work?
When you describe those periods where you feel that heavy, flat feeling and like a failed version of yourself, how long do those stretches typically last? Are we talking about days, weeks, or longer?

Well, um... if you look at the whole picture, like over the entire time I've had these ups and downs, I guess all those low, withdrawn periods have added up to... maybe about seven months total? 

I mean, it's definitely not all at once! Just, you know, a few weeks here or there that sort of accumulate over time. I really try my best to push through it and not let it affect my team or my marriage, so I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just sitting around doing nothing for months on end. I'd hate for you to think I'm just being lazy or not trying. 

Is... is that kind of timeline helpful for what you need to know? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right details.

When you have one of those low, flat periods you mentioned, does it tend to last for a few weeks or more at a stretch before you start feeling better? Or is it more like the low mood comes and goes throughout each day or week?

Um, well, when it hits, it usually sticks around for a while. Like... maybe a few months at a stretch, if I'm being honest. It doesn't really come and go day to day. It just sort of settles in. 

I guess the main thing is... well, I just stop doing the things I usually love. Like, I used to really look forward to grilling on the weekends, or going indoor climbing, or playing music at church. I even mentor the high school robotics kids, which I normally think is just the best thing. But during those long stretches, I just... I kind of stop caring about any of it. I'll see their messages asking for help or asking to hang out, and I just let them sit there unanswered. 

I feel terrible admitting that, because I know people are counting on me and I really don't want to let anyone down. I know I should just push through and go anyway. Does that make sense? I hope that's not too unusual or... or disappointing to hear.
When you're in one of those low periods that lasts a few months, is that one continuous stretch of feeling down, or does it break up into separate episodes with some better days or weeks in between?

Well, um... I guess I'm not entirely sure how to answer that. I mean, it's not like I'm tracking every single day on a calendar or anything. I try to stay positive and just keep moving forward, you know? 

I suppose... well, I don't really know if it's one long, unbroken stretch or if there are little breaks in there. I'd like to think I have some good days mixed in, because I really do try to snap out of it. I don't want to be difficult or give you the wrong impression. I just... I haven't really paid that close attention to whether it's continuous or broken up. Is it okay if I don't have a perfectly clear answer for that one? I want to be helpful, I just don't want to guess and tell you the wrong thing.

When you think back over the past year or two, can you describe how many separate times you've had one of those low, flat periods? Like, how many different times did it start and then eventually lift?

Um, gosh... I really haven't kept a strict count. I mean, I try not to dwell on the negative times too much, so I just sort of push past them when they lift. 

If I had to guess... I don't know, maybe a few times? But honestly, I'm just not certain how many separate times it's happened over the last year or two. I really wish I had a better answer for you. I should probably be keeping a journal or something, shouldn't I? I just... I haven't really tracked the exact number of times. Is it alright if I just say I'm not really sure?

When you're in one of those high-energy, really driven periods you mentioned at the beginning—where you're launching lots of projects and feeling very motivated—how much sleep do you typically need during those times? Do you feel rested on just a few hours of sleep, or do you still feel like you need your normal amount?

Well, um, when I get like that, I actually don't need a whole lot of sleep. I hope that doesn't sound too strange. But, yeah, there have been these runs where I'll sleep maybe... maybe three hours? And then I'll wake up sharp at 3 or 4 a.m., and I don't feel tired at all. It's actually kind of nice, like I've been handed bonus time to get things done, you know? 

I know you're supposed to get eight hours, and I really do try to have good habits most of the time. But during those stretches, I just feel completely rested on those few hours. Is that... is that something I should be worried about? I just want to make sure I'm not doing anything wrong by taking advantage of the extra time.

During one of those low periods you mentioned, when it does eventually lift and you start feeling better, how quickly does that happen? Does the mood improve over a day or two, or does it take longer—like a week or more—before you feel like yourself again?

Um, well, when it starts to get better... I guess I haven't really timed it exactly. I try to just be grateful when the fog starts lifting, you know? 

I don't think it's like flipping a switch in a day or two, but... I also don't want to make it sound like it drags on forever once it starts improving. Maybe it's somewhere in the middle? I just sort of realize one day that things feel a little lighter, and I try to focus on that instead of analyzing how long it took. 

I'm sorry, I know that's another vague answer. I really am trying to give you the information you need. Is it okay if I'm just not totally sure how fast the transition is? I hope I'm not being too frustrating.
When one of those low periods starts to lift, and you begin feeling better, would you say it takes at least two weeks before you're back to feeling like your normal self again?

Um, I'm really not sure if it takes a full two weeks. I mean, once I start feeling a bit better, I just try to focus on that positive momentum, you know? I don't really mark it on a calendar or anything. 

I guess it could take that long sometimes, but I wouldn't want to say for sure and give you the wrong idea. I just... I try to be happy that it's going away. Does that make sense? I hope it's okay that I don't have a more exact timeline for you. I'm really trying to be helpful, I promise.
When you think back to the last time you were in one of those low, flat periods, roughly how many weeks did that particular stretch last before you started feeling better?

Um, well, the last time... I guess if you add up all the time I've spent in those really low, withdrawn periods over the whole course of this... it's probably been around seven months total. 

I know that sounds like a really long time, and I don't want you to think I'm just wallowing in it or not trying to get better. I really do try to push through it. It's just that sometimes it's so hard to shake. 

Is that... is seven months a really bad sign? I hope I'm not a hopeless case or anything. I just want to be honest with you so you can help me, but I don't want to sound like I'm not putting in the effort to stay positive.

When you think about those low periods over the past couple of years, do they feel like separate times when the depression starts and then goes away completely before it comes back again? Or is it more like the low mood is always kind of there in the background, just getting worse and better at different times?

Um, I think... well, it's not like it's always there, weighing me down completely. I really don't want to sound like I'm just miserable all the time, because I'm not. I have good days! 

But I guess... maybe it doesn't always go away one hundred percent? Like, sometimes it feels like it's completely gone, and I'm doing great, but other times it might just be sort of... hovering a little bit? Just in the background. But I really try not to let it get to me when it's like that. I try to stay busy and keep a good attitude. 

I don't know if that's the right way to describe it. Is it normal for it to kind of linger a little bit, or should it be completely gone? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture, but I also want you to know I'm really trying my best to manage it when it's there.

When you're not in one of those low periods, and you're feeling better, does the depression completely go away and stay away until the next low period starts? Or is there always at least a little bit of that flat or heavy feeling lingering underneath, even on your better days?

Um, I guess it's kind of like what I was just trying to explain... I really don't think it's always there underneath. I mean, when I'm feeling better, I really do feel good! I go to work, I manage my IT team, and I just try to be as productive and positive as I can be. 

But if you're asking if every single drop of it is completely gone... I honestly don't know for sure. It's hard to tell if it's one hundred percent away or just... really, really quiet? I don't really focus on it because I'm just so relieved to be having good days again, you know? 

I hope it's alright that I don't have a perfectly clear answer for you on that. I just don't want to say it's always lingering and make it sound like I'm not doing well, because I really am putting in the effort to stay on top of things. Is that... does that help at all?

When you're in one of those really driven, high-energy periods with lots of projects and less sleep, does that energetic feeling come on suddenly after you've been in a low period? Or does it build up gradually while you're still feeling some of that flatness?

Um, well... I guess I'm not totally sure how to answer that one. I haven't really... paid super close attention to exactly how the transition happens, to be honest. 

When I get into those really productive phases, I'm just so focused on work and getting things done for my team that I don't really stop to analyze how it started. I just try to ride that wave of good energy and make the most of it, you know? It's actually a really great time for my career when that happens. 

I'm sorry I don't have a better timeline for you on that. I hope that's okay? I just don't want to make something up if I haven't really noticed a specific pattern of whether it's sudden or gradual. I'm really trying to give you the most accurate information I can. Is it... is it pretty common for people not to notice exactly how those shifts happen?

When you're in one of those really driven, energetic periods with lots of projects and less sleep, and then it eventually ends, what happens next? Do you go directly into one of those low, flat periods? Or do you have a stretch of time where you feel pretty normal and stable before the low mood kicks in?

Um, well... I guess I haven't really tracked exactly what happens right after the energy drops off. I really wish I had a better memory for this kind of thing, I'm sorry. 

I think... maybe it just depends? Like, sometimes I might feel okay for a bit, just kind of catching my breath after working so hard. But honestly, I'm usually just trying so hard to keep everything running smoothly at work that I don't really stop to check if I'm feeling totally normal or if the low mood is starting to creep in. 

I just... I try to push through it and be a good manager, no matter what part of the cycle I'm in. I hope it's okay that I don't have a perfectly clear timeline for you. Is it normal to kind of lose track of the days when you're just trying to stay productive? I really want to be helpful, I just don't want to guess and give you the wrong idea.
When you think about the last time you had one of those low, flat periods, roughly how many weeks or months did that one particular stretch last before you started feeling noticeably better?

Um, well... if I think about the whole time this has been going on... I guess if you add all those low periods together, it probably comes out to around seven months total. 

I know that sounds like a long time when you put it all together like that, but it wasn't all at once! I really do bounce back, and I always make sure I get back to work and take care of my team. I just don't want you to think I've been sitting around doing nothing for seven months straight, because I really do push myself to keep going. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have the exact number of weeks for just that last time... I just know the total is around seven months. Does that make sense? I'm really trying to give you the right picture here.
When you think back to one specific low period—not adding them all up together—how many weeks did that one particular stretch last from when it started until you felt noticeably better?

Um, let me think... just one specific time... 

I guess... maybe a couple of weeks? Or maybe three? It's really hard to separate them out in my head, I'm sorry. I just try so hard not to dwell on those times, you know? When I'm in it, I just try to put my head down and get through it so I can get back to being productive. I don't really mark it on a calendar or anything. 

I feel like if I focus too much on how long I'm feeling down, it just makes it worse, and I really need to be there for my team. I hope two or three weeks sounds about right? I'm sorry I can't be more precise... I just really try to push past those periods as quickly as I can. Is it okay that I'm a little fuzzy on the exact number of weeks?
When you're in one of those low periods, from the moment it starts until you begin feeling noticeably better, would you say it typically lasts at least two weeks?

Um, yeah, I guess I'd say it definitely lasts at least two weeks. Usually longer, if I'm being completely honest. 

It's just... during those stretches, I wake up and I just feel like this... this totally failed version of myself. Everything just feels so heavy and flat. Even when my wife asks me completely normal things, like what I want for dinner or how work was, it just feels like... like it's too much effort to even form the words to answer her. 

I try really hard not to let it show, though. I don't want her to worry, and I definitely don't want to be a burden on her or my team at work. I always try to put on a brave face, you know? I hope that makes sense. Is it normal to feel that kind of heaviness for a couple of weeks at a time? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

When you're in one of those low periods and feeling that heaviness and flatness, does it stay that way continuously for those couple of weeks or longer? Or do you have days mixed in where you feel a bit better before it gets heavy again?

Um, well... I guess when I'm in it, it's pretty much all the time. It doesn't really let up. 

Like I said, I just wake up and there's this... this awful feeling that I'm just a completely failed version of myself. And it just stays there. It's just heavy and flat, day after day. And, um, like I mentioned with my wife... even answering her when she asks about my day or dinner... it just feels like climbing a mountain just to get the words out. 

But I really, really try not to let it drag down the whole house, you know? I still try to sit at the table and be present, even if I'm not saying much. I just don't want to be the guy who ruins everyone's day because he can't snap out of it. 

So, yeah, it's pretty continuous for those weeks. I hope I'm explaining that okay? I just want to make sure I'm answering exactly what you're asking.

Between those low periods that last a couple of weeks or more, when you're feeling better and back to your normal self, how long does that stretch of feeling good typically last before the next low period starts?

Um, gosh, that's a really good question... I'm sorry, I don't actually know the exact answer to that. 

When I'm finally feeling better and back to myself, I just... I throw myself completely into my work and my family. I really try to make up for the time I lost when I was down, you know? So I don't really keep track of how long the good stretches last. I just ride that wave of being productive and try to be the best manager and husband I can be for as long as it stays. 

I haven't really measured it on a calendar or anything, so it's hard to say if it's months or what. I'm really sorry I don't have a more specific timeframe for you... is it okay that I'm not sure about that part? I can try to start keeping track if that would be helpful for you.

When you're not in one of those low periods and you're feeling better, would you say you feel just normal and stable, or do you feel unusually energetic, driven, and like you're accomplishing a lot more than usual?

Um, well, when I'm out of the low periods, I definitely feel, um, very productive. Like I said, I really try to make up for lost time. 

I wouldn't say it's, like, abnormal or anything bad, but I do get a lot done. I'll be pacing around the house with my laptop, trying to get ahead on work, or I'll suddenly decide to completely reorganize the garage on a Saturday. I'll rewrite all my project boards at work to make them perfectly efficient. It's just... I have so much energy then. 

Actually, if I try to just sit down and watch a TV show with my wife during those times, I get this... this weird physical discomfort. Like I just can't sit still, I have to be doing something useful. 

But it's a good thing, right? Being productive and getting things in order? I just figure it's me being a good provider and manager. Does that sound like what you're asking about? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is, I just really like to be on top of things when I have the energy for it.
